paragraphs.notes: Whole page body is a single un-numbered continuation of the Markush substituent enumeration inside the Patentansprueche. The claims begin on printed page 79 (PDF p81) with 'Patentansprueche:' and claim 1; no new claim number and no new symbol heading starts on this page, so the symbol this list belongs to is fixed on an earlier page. WO A1 publications carry no [00NN] paragraph markers, so marker is null. The page opens mid-term: printed page 83 (PDF p85) ends on 'Cycloalkyl-' and this page begins with the lower-case tail 'alkinyloxycarbonylamino,', so the term that straddles the page break is Cycloalkylalkinyloxycarbonylamino. The tail is transcribed here as printed, lower case and without the 'Cycloalkyl' head, so the two pages can be joined downstream without either page inventing text it does not carry. The page ends on 'Halogenalkenylcarbonyl,' with the list still open, continuing onto printed page 85 (PDF p87). LINE-BREAK JOINING: the 34 printed lines are flowed into one string; lines are joined with a single space, except where a line ends in a hyphen, where the next line is joined with no space and the printed hyphen is kept. Four lines end in a hyphen: 'Cycloalkylalkinyloxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-' + 'amino', 'Cycloalkenylalkoxy-carbonyl-N-alkyl-' + 'amino', 'Cyclo-' + 'alkenylalkinyloxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino', and 'N-Alkylheteroaryl-alkinyloxycarbonyl-N-' + 'alkyl-amino'. ONE OF THOSE FOUR IS AMBIGUOUS AND IS DELIBERATELY LEFT AS PRINTED: 'Cyclo-' + 'alkenylalkinyloxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' yields 'Cyclo-alkenylalkinyloxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' with a hyphen after 'Cyclo', where the same head is printed unbroken and unhyphenated elsewhere on this page ('Cycloalkenylalkinyloxycarbonylamino' on line 3, 'Cycloalkenylalkinyloxycarbonyloxy' on line 13). The hyphen may therefore be line-break hyphenation rather than part of the name. It has not been deleted, because this page also prints two spurious mid-line hyphens of exactly that shape in the same block ('Cycloalkyl-alkoxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' and 'Cycloalkenylalkoxy-carbonyl-N-alkyl-amino'), so the two readings cannot be told apart from the page and no character printed on the page has been removed. A consumer that needs the unbroken term should read it as Cycloalkenylalkinyloxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino. SIX IRREGULARITIES READ AS PRINTED AND DELIBERATELY NOT CORRECTED. (1) The 'alkinyl' stem loses its final 'l' in eight terms, in every case after Aryl, Heteroaryl or Heterocyclyl: Arylalkinyoxycarbonylamino, Heteroarylalkinyoxycarbonylamino, Heterocyclylalkinyoxycarbonylamino, Arylalkinyoxycarbonyloxy, Heteroarylalkinyoxycarbonyloxy, Heterocyclylalkinyoxycarbonyloxy, Arylalkinyoxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino and Heterocyclylalkinyoxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino. Verified at 3x and 4x on each of the eight: the glyphs read n-y-o-x-y, with no 'l'. The parallel Cycloalkyl and Cycloalkenyl members on the same page keep the 'l' (Cycloalkenylalkinyloxycarbonylamino, Cycloalkylalkinyloxycarbonyloxy, Cycloalkenylalkinyloxycarbonyloxy, Cycloalkylalkinyloxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino), and printed page 83 (PDF p85) prints 'Arylalkinyloxycarbonyl' with the 'l', so the loss is internal to this page and is not a house spelling. The missing letter has not been supplied. (2) The N-alkyl-amino block opens with two members that carry no '-N-alkyl-': the line reads 'Alkoxycarbonylamino, Alkenyloxycarbonylamino, Alkinyloxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino,'. The first two duplicate entries already printed on page 83; only the third member of the series carries the N-alkyl. Verified at 2.5x. Nothing has been inserted. (3) 'Cycloalkyl-alkoxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' carries a hyphen after 'Cycloalkyl' where the neighbouring 'Cycloalkoxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' and 'Cycloalkylalkenyloxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' do not; the hyphen is mid-line, not at a line end. (4) 'Cycloalkenylalkoxy-carbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' is hyphenated between 'alkoxy' and 'carbonyl', where every parallel member is unhyphenated there. (5) The Aryl series of the N-alkyl-amino block runs 'Arylalkinyoxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino, Heteroarylalkoxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' with no 'Heteroaryloxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' between them, although the Aryl branch two items earlier does carry its 'Aryloxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino'. Two further members of the same block break the parallel the other way by carrying a leading 'N-Alkyl' that no neighbour has: 'N-Alkylheteroaryl-alkinyloxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' and 'N-Alkylheterocyclylalkoxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino'. Verified at 2.5x. Nothing has been inserted. (6) 'Heterocyclylalkenyloxycarbonyl-amino' ends the block without the '-N-alkyl-' its immediate neighbour 'Heterocyclylalkinyoxycarbonyl-N-alkyl-amino' carries, and hyphenates the final 'amino'. Transcribed exactly as printed. The en field is a translation, not a copy: these are GERMAN group names, and German 'Alkinyl' is English 'alkynyl' and German 'Halogen-' is English 'halo-' throughout, so 'Halogenalkoxy' is 'haloalkoxy'. German noun capitalisation is dropped in en; the 'N-' locant prefix keeps its capital N. The six irregularities above are carried through into en unchanged: the eight terms missing the 'l' are rendered 'alkynyoxy', preserving both the German-to-English i/y change and the missing letter, and the ambiguous 'cyclo-' hyphen is kept. A small stray ink speckle sits above the line beginning 'Arylalkoxycarbonylamino', in the right margin area; the same mark appears at the same place on the neighbouring pages (PDF p80, p81, p85), so it is scanner dirt, not a printed character. There is no footer and the page below the last printed line is blank.
